name: Georgia Theatre
unique: A 1911 movie house turned rock club on Athens' main square, rebuilt after a 2009 fire, with a rooftop bar and a schedule that still breaks national acts.
buzz: The room sounds good and the roof is the pre show move. Check the calendar, because the good shows sell out.

name: 40 Watt Club
unique: The club where R.E.M., the B-52's and Neutral Milk Hotel came up, still a low ceiling room with a sticky floor and a booking policy that favors the next thing.
buzz: It is a dive in the best sense. Cash bar, no glamour, and the sound is loud enough to feel in your chest.

name: State Botanical Garden of Georgia
unique: A 313 acre garden with a conservatory, a formal rose garden, woodland trails and a children's garden, run by the university and free most days.
buzz: The conservatory is the rainy day win and the trails are shaded. Parking is free but the lot fills on spring weekends.

name: Double Barreled Cannon
unique: A Civil War cannon designed to fire two balls linked by a chain, which never worked, now standing on the courthouse corner as a monument to a bad idea.
buzz: It takes five minutes and the plaque is the fun part. Pair it with the downtown walk.

name: Augusta Canal
unique: A 19th century industrial canal with a towpath trail, restored mills and a electric boat tour that explains how Augusta powered itself before the Civil War.
buzz: The towpath is flat and shady, good for bikes and strollers. The boat tour is the way to hear the history.

name: Phinizy Swamp Nature Park
unique: A 1,100 acre wetland nature park with boardwalks and dikes through a working water treatment landscape, where herons, alligators and wintering ducks show up close.
buzz: It sounds industrial and is actually beautiful, with more wildlife than most parks. Bring binoculars and bug spray.

name: Morris Museum of Art
unique: The first museum devoted to Southern art, with landscapes, portraits and contemporary work from the region, on Augusta's riverfront.
buzz: A serious collection in a small city, and the riverfront location makes a good afternoon. Check for free days.

name: Jekyll Island
unique: A barrier island with a millionaire's club historic district, driftwood beaches, a turtle center and 20 miles of bike trails under live oaks.
buzz: The parking fee is the only gate and the island never feels crowded. Rent bikes, see the turtle hospital, and stay for the sunset on Driftwood Beach.

name: St. Simons Island
unique: An island of live oak canopies, a working lighthouse, a village pier and the ruins of Fort Frederica, with shrimp boats and a beach at the south end.
buzz: Park once and walk or bike. The lighthouse climb is worth it, and the crab shack near the pier is the local lunch.

name: Hofwyl-Broadfield Plantation
unique: A rice plantation house preserved with its original furniture, live oaks and marsh, telling the story of five generations and the enslaved people who built the rice fields.
buzz: The house tour is intimate and the grounds are quiet. The marsh boardwalk is a good birding stop.

name: Berry College
unique: A 27,000 acre campus with a Gothic stone chapel, a working farm, deer and trails, often called the largest campus in the world.
buzz: The chapel and the oak allee are the photo stops, and the trails are open to the public. Drive the loop at dusk for deer.

name: Chieftains Museum
unique: The home of Major Ridge, a Cherokee leader who signed the treaty that led to the Trail of Tears, with Cherokee artifacts and the story told from his side.
buzz: A small museum with a complicated story, told well. The house itself is the exhibit.

name: Myrtle Hill Cemetery
unique: A terraced cemetery on a hill above the confluence of two rivers, with Confederate graves, a monumental arch and a view over Rome.
buzz: The climb is steep and the view is the reward. Quiet, free and good with the Chieftains museum nearby.

name: Old Governor's Mansion
unique: The Greek Revival mansion where Georgia's governors lived before Atlanta, restored to its 1850s appearance, with the slave quarters and the story of the household included.
buzz: The guided tour is excellent and honest about the enslaved staff. The staircase and the dome are the showpieces.

name: Andalusia
unique: Flannery O'Connor's farm, where she wrote her short stories and raised peacocks, with the house, the dairy barn and the birds still on the property.
buzz: Pilgrimage for readers, and the peacocks are a hit with everyone else. The house tour is small and personal.

name: Milledgeville Historic District
unique: A full antebellum grid of churches, mansions and a Gothic revival asylum, in the town that was Georgia's capital from 1804 to 1868.
buzz: The architecture is the draw and the town is quiet. Pick up a walking tour map and look up at the windows.

name: The Big Oak
unique: A live oak said to be over 300 years old, with a 165 foot canopy, standing in the middle of a residential street and held up by cables and love.
buzz: It is a tree, and people photograph it for twenty minutes. The neighborhood around it is worth the walk.

name: Pebble Hill Plantation
unique: A quail hunting plantation with a 1930s main house, a carriage museum, dog cemeteries and sporting art, in the red hills of south Georgia.
buzz: The house tour and the grounds are both good, and the sporting art is unusual. Check the season before driving out.

name: Jack Hadley Black History Museum
unique: A collection of photographs, military records and family histories of Black Thomasville, assembled by a local historian over decades.
buzz: Personal and specific, with stories you will not find in a state museum. Call ahead for group tours.

name: Consolidated Gold Mine
unique: A guided walk into a real 19th century gold mine, with underground tunnels, mining equipment and a panning trough where you keep what you find.
buzz: The underground tour is cool in summer and the guides are funny. Panning is the kid highlight and the gold is real, if tiny.

name: Dahlonega Gold Museum
unique: A museum in the 1836 courthouse on the square, covering the first American gold rush, the mint that coined it and the Cherokee removal that followed.
buzz: The gold rush story is the surprise for most visitors, and the building is worth the stop.

name: Blue Ridge Scenic Railway
unique: A four hour round trip on a heritage railroad along the Toccoa River, with an hour stop in the twin towns of McCaysville and Copperhill.
buzz: Book the open air car and sit on the river side. The layover is long enough for lunch and short enough to stay fun.

name: Mercier Orchards
unique: A fourth generation apple orchard with u-pick apples and berries, a bakery, a hard cider tasting room and a market full of fried pies.
buzz: The fried pies and cider doughnuts are the reason, and u-pick is a fall ritual. Go early on October weekends.

name: Hillcrest Orchards
unique: An apple orchard with u-pick, a petting farm, a corn maze, a bakery and hard cider, built for a full family afternoon in the north Georgia hills.
buzz: It is busy and commercial and kids love it. The apple cider slushie is the local tradition.

name: Georgia Apple Festival
unique: A two weekend street festival with hundreds of craft vendors, apple pies, cider, a parade and a car show, in the self proclaimed apple capital of Georgia.
buzz: Go early for parking and pie. It is crowded, hot and exactly what an apple festival should be.

name: Anna Ruby Falls
unique: Twin waterfalls dropping 150 feet side by side, reached by a paved half mile trail through hemlock and rhododendron in the Chattahoochee forest.
buzz: The trail is steep in spots but paved, and the falls are loud after rain. Go early to beat the Helen crowds.

name: Unicoi State Park
unique: A state park with a lake, a beach, paddleboard rentals, zip lines and trails that connect to Anna Ruby Falls, minutes from the Alpine village of Helen.
buzz: The lake is the summer draw and the zip line is the surprise. Book cabins early for October.

name: Okefenokee Swamp Park
unique: A private gateway to the Okefenokee with boat tours, a boardwalk, a wildlife exhibit and a train, where alligators and cypress trees are within arm's reach of the rail.
buzz: The boat tour is the way to see it, and the gators are guaranteed in warm months. Bring sunscreen and bug spray.

name: Southern Forest World
unique: A museum of the southern pine forest with a walk through a simulated swamp, logging equipment and the story of the turpentine and pulp industries.
buzz: Small and old fashioned, with a great snake exhibit. A good rainy day stop with kids.

name: Stephen C. Foster State Park
unique: A state park inside the Okefenokee wilderness, reached by a long dirt road, with canoe rentals, guided boat trips and dark skies for stargazing.
buzz: Remote in the best way, with cypress tunnels and almost no light pollution. Book canoe trips ahead and bring food.
